term: income tax relief
definition: Income tax relief refers to the government’s specific deductions or exemptions to taxpayers to reduce their taxable income. These reliefs are designed to incentivise certain behaviours or circumstances that contribute to the overall well-being of individuals or society. Tax residents can only claim tax relief, including non-Singapore Citizens who spend more than 183 days in Singapore within a year.  Source: Income tax relief  https://www.99.co/singapore/glossary/income-tax-relief/  (index: Income tax relief)

term: types of income tax reliefs available in Singapore
definition: • Earned Income Relief This relief is intended for individuals actively employed or involved in a trade, business, profession, or vocation to earn income. • Spouse/Handicapped Spouse Relief This relief acknowledges the contribution of taxpayers, regardless of gender, who have provided support to their spouses. • Foreign Domestic Worker Levy Relief The FDWL Relief is provided as an incentive to encourage married women to remain active in the workforce. This relief is exclusive to married women; singles and married men are ineligible for FDWL Relief. • CPF Relief for Employees The CPF Relief is granted to motivate individuals to save for retirement. It can be claimed by employees who are either Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents. • CPF Relief for Self-Employed Self-employed individuals who also work as employees can receive relief on their CPF contributions, which helps reduce the tax they must pay. • NSman (Self) Relief All eligible NSmen who are operationally ready National Servicemen are eligible for NSman tax relief. This relief is provided to acknowledge their contributions to National Service. The NSman Relief is based on the national service performed in the preceding work year. In addition, NSman Wife Relief and NSman Parent Relief are also granted to the wives and parents of NSmen, respectively. These reliefs are given to recognise the support they provide to their husbands and sons who are serving in National Service. • NSman (Wife) Relief • NSman (Parent) Relief • Parent/Handicapped Parent Relief This relief is provided to encourage and acknowledge individuals fulfilling their responsibilities towards supporting their parents, grandparents, parents-in-law, or grandparents-in-law in Singapore. It aims to promote the value of filial piety and recognise the efforts made by individuals in caring for and providing financial support to their elderly family members. • Grandparent Caregiver Relief GCR is provided to working mothers who enlist the assistance of their parents, grandparents, parents-in-law, or grandparents-in-law (including those of former spouses) to provide care for their children. • Qualifying/Handicapped Child Relief Parents are provided QCR and HCR to acknowledge and appreciate their dedication to caring for their children. These reliefs are designed to recognise parents’ financial responsibilities and efforts in raising and providing for their children. • Working Mother’s Child Relief WMCR is granted to achieve the following objectives: • Promote the continued participation of married women in the workforce even after becoming parents. • Encourage parents to choose Singapore Citizenship for their children. • Recognise and provide incentives for families with children who hold Singapore Citizenship. • Handicapped Brother/Sister Relief This relief is for those who support and care for their siblings and siblings-in-law with disabilities or special needs. Additionally, there are other reliefs that individuals can claim if they meet the eligibility criteria: • Life Insurance Relief • Course Fees Relief • SRS Relief • CPF Cash Top-up Relief • CPF Relief (Compulsory and Voluntary Medisave Contributions)  Source: Income tax relief  https://www.99.co/singapore/glossary/income-tax-relief/  (index: Income tax relief)

term: What is Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR)?
definition: The Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR) is a home loan limit implemented by MAS (Monetary Authority of Singapore) that applies to public and private properties. The TDSR establishes boundaries on the maximum borrowing capacity for homebuyers. It is currently set at 55% (as of 16 Dec 2021) of their gross monthly income. The primary objective is to promote responsible borrowing among households and enhance the credit evaluation standards of financial institutions. It’s important to note that the TDSR is a permanent requirement that all banks and financial institutions must adhere to when assessing various types of loans, including housing loans, refinancing of housing loans, and loans secured by property.  Source: Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR)  https://www.99.co/singapore/glossary/total-debt-servicing-ratio-tdsr/  (index: Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR))
aliases: What is Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR)?|Total Debt Servicing Ratio|TDSR

term: What does the Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR) do
definition: The implementation of the Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR) is essential for various reasons, as follows: The TDSR promotes higher standards in credit evaluation by financial institutions. It encourages lenders to adopt more thorough assessment practices, reducing the lending risk to borrowers struggling to meet their repayment obligations. The TDSR acts as a safeguard to prevent borrowers from becoming overly indebted. It promotes financial prudence by encouraging individuals to consider their financial capabilities and make responsible decisions when taking on property loans. By preventing borrowers from becoming over-leveraged, the TDSR contributes to the long-term stability of the property market. It helps prevent speculative behaviour and excessive borrowing, reducing the likelihood of market volatility and potential financial crises.  Source: Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR)  https://www.99.co/singapore/glossary/total-debt-servicing-ratio-tdsr/  (index: Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR))

term: How to calculate Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR)
definition: You can use the following formula to calculate your TDSR: (Total monthly debt obligations of the borrower / Gross monthly income of the borrower) x 100% The numerator of the TDSR formula represents the borrower’s monthly debt obligations, which include various types of outstanding debts, such as property loans (including the loan being applied for), car loans, student loans, renovation loans, and so on. Financial institutions have the responsibility of accurately calculating and verifying these debt obligations by: • Collecting relevant supporting documents from the borrower • Cross-referencing the information with the credit bureau to ensure accuracy The information provided was accurate at the time of publication. For the latest changes and updates, head over to the official websites.  Source: Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR)  https://www.99.co/singapore/glossary/total-debt-servicing-ratio-tdsr/  (index: Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR))

term: Basics of the COE System
definition: • The COE is essentially a license that allows you to own and use a vehicle in Singapore for 10 years. After this period, you either need to deregister your vehicle or renew the COE to continue using the vehicle. • Category A: For cars up to 1,600cc and 130bhp. • Category B: For cars above 1,600cc or 130bhp. • Category C: For goods vehicles and buses. • Category D: For motorcycles. • Category E: Open category, which can be used for any vehicle type except motorcycles and is often used for luxury cars. • The Land Transport Authority (LTA) determines the number of COEs available each month, known as the COE quota. This quota is based on several factors, including vehicle de-registrations and the government’s target vehicle population.  Source: COE Bidding System, Process, How to Renew [2024 Guide]  https://www.99.co/singapore/glossary/coe-bidding-system/  (index: COE Bidding System, Process, How to Renew [2024 Guide])

term: COE Bidding Process
definition: • COE bidding exercises are conducted twice a month, usually on the first and third Monday. The bidding period lasts for three days, from Monday to Wednesday. • Step 1: Submission of Bids Bidders, who are often car dealers or individual buyers, submit their bids electronically through the LTA’s online system. Each bid must meet the minimum reserve price set by the LTA. • Bidders, who are often car dealers or individual buyers, submit their bids electronically through the LTA’s online system. Each bid must meet the minimum reserve price set by the LTA. • Step 2: Price Movements As bids are placed, the COE price fluctuates. Bidders can adjust their bids to stay competitive. • As bids are placed, the COE price fluctuates. Bidders can adjust their bids to stay competitive. • Step 3: Closing and Results Once the bidding period closes, the COE prices are finalized. The highest unsuccessful bid determines the COE price, and successful bidders pay the price they offered. Results are typically announced shortly after the bidding closes on Wednesday. • Once the bidding period closes, the COE prices are finalized. The highest unsuccessful bid determines the COE price, and successful bidders pay the price they offered. Results are typically announced shortly after the bidding closes on Wednesday. • Successful bidders must pay the COE price they bid, and the COE is valid for 10 years. After this period, it can be renewed by paying the Prevailing Quota Premium (PQP), which is an average of the COE prices in the preceding three months. • Vehicle owners can renew their COE by paying the PQP before the COE expires. You can choose to renew it for 5 or 10 years. COEs can also be transferred to another person, though this is more common with company-owned vehicles. term: How to Renew Your COE
definition: When your COE is nearing its 10-year expiration, you can either deregister your vehicle or renew your COE for another 5 or 10 years. Here’s how you can renew your COE: • 5-Year Renewal: Suitable if you’re uncertain about keeping the vehicle long-term. After renewing for 5 years, you cannot renew the COE again and must deregister the vehicle. • 10-Year Renewal: Ideal if you plan to keep your vehicle for a long time. You can continue renewing every 10 years. • The PQP is the average of the COE prices over the last three months. You can find the latest PQP on the LTA website or through your vehicle dealer. • Payments are typically made online through the LTA’s One Motoring portal. Ensure you renew before your COE expires to avoid penalties or losing your vehicle. • Once payment is complete, your COE will be renewed for the chosen period, all done online without needing to visit any office.  Source: COE Bidding System, Process, How to Renew [2024 Guide]  https://www.99.co/singapore/glossary/coe-bidding-system/  (index: COE Bidding System, Process, How to Renew [2024 Guide])

definition: It’s essential to stay informed about COE prices and bidding results, especially if you’re planning to buy a car or renew your COE soon. You can check the latest prices on the LTA website, through news outlets, or by contacting your car dealer. Knowing the trends will help you make informed decisions and potentially save money by timing your purchase or renewal when prices are more favorable. The COE system plays a crucial role in regulating the number of vehicles on Singapore’s roads. By understanding how it works and staying updated on the latest prices, you can better navigate the complexities of vehicle ownership in Singapore.
